newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Floods in central and northern Sweden recede.
newsitem.headline: Floods in central and northern Sweden recede.

text.p: Floodwaters were receding in northern Sweden on Wednesday and forecast light showers were not expected to worsen the situation, while floods in central Sweden had ended, emergency services officials said.
"The situation (in the north) is more stable," fire brigade spokesman Hans-Eric Norberg told Reuters.
"In some parts the water level is falling quite rapidly. In large water bodies, such as lakes, the water level is only decreasing slowly and in some places not at all."
Heavy rainfall of up to 265 mm, which started on Sunday and continued on Monday, caused patchy flooding in the counties of Norrbotten and Vasterbotten.

Floods damaged roads, between 20 and 30 houses, and swept away two small bridges in a sparsely-populated, 20 square km area outside the northern city of Pitea, about 900 km (550 miles) north of Stockholm.
Rescue workers evacuated about 20 people, mostly elderly, from their homes by helicopter and boat earlier this week after the flooding left them isolated. No deaths or injuries were reported.
Victoria Lundberg, who refused to be evacuated with her three small children, was in good spirits on Wednesday.
"We live in a high place and we are not flooded any more. But we can't go anywhere, we're still cut off," she told Reuters by telephone from her isolated house.
"It's been a grand drama. All streams have become rivers, all ditches streams and swamps have become lakes."
The rescue services called in six military tanks on Wednesday to help people still in the area but the rain was expected to subside.

"There might be some showers today but they won't be heavy," said Maud Nilsson, a hydrologist at Sweden's weather service SMHI. "There hasn't been much rain overnight and the water should disappear in a couple of days."

Floods in central Sweden, which closed some minor roads near the Swedish town of Flen, about 220 km (140 miles) west of Stockholm earlier this week, had already receded, the local rescue service said.
